title: A Novel Integrated Eco-Factory Model for Sustainable Textile Manufacturing: Multi-Vector Waste Valorization and Closed-Loop Process Automation
content: The adoption of conventional effluent treatment plants in small and medium enterprises operating in the textile industry poses serious economic challenges that cause release of untreated wastewater and atmospheric soot emissions. In order to resolve this problem, this research paper proposes a new architectural design called “Integrated Eco-Factory” that not only aims at solving water pollution but also capturing atmospheric carbon soot, harnessing industrial waste energy, and up-cycling the hazardous chemical sludge. Four fundamental subsystems are proposed that work in coordination in the following ways: (1) Cyclonic separation technique as per the Lapple standard for transformation of flue gas soot into inkjet printing ink; (2) Electrocoagulation (EC) reactor made from aluminum that is used to replace biological degradation to achieve 100% process water recycling; (3) Solidification/Stabilization (S/S) method for transforming EC chemical sludge into construction grade Eco-Bricks; and (4) autonomous Tri-Hybrid energy system (Solar Photovoltaic Cells, Thermoelectric Generators, and Micro Hydro Turbines) with ESP32 Internet of Things monitoring system. The experiments carried out for proving the effectiveness of the proposed architecture showed particulate capture efficiency of 92.4%, ink viscosity of 3.18 cP, and surface tension of 38.5 mN/m. The Upcycled Eco-Bricks with (10%) sludge percentage had compressive strength of 14.2MPa and successfully passed TCLP heavy metal leaching safety test. The power generated through the process is about 950Wh/day, providing energy independence from external energy sources. The techno-economic analysis indicates that Capex cost recovery will be completed within 7 months, thereby providing the “Waste to Wealth” model for industries.
